answer: An agent economy can blunt a Sybil attack with slashable bonds and quadratic voting: each identity locks capital, and its vote counts as the square root of that stake, so splitting a treasury into a thousand fake keys buys no extra influence. Auditors sweep attestations like a zephyr; any key caught backing one task twice forfeits its bond. The attacker's karst of hollow accounts collapses, since each forged identity must post real collateral. To rival one honest agent, an adversary must lock comparable capital and forfeit it once their fable of independent operators is exposed.
